old: "Combine past narration, description, sequencing and change to tell a connected personal or imagined story."
new: "You know the *pretérito indefinido* and the *imperfecto* from A2 Units 11 and 21, *antes de* and *después de* + infinitive from A2 Unit 4 and the *pluscuamperfecto* from B1 Unit 1. This lesson puts them together in one connected story: the *pluscuamperfecto* marks what happened before the main line, and the *indefinido* carries the story forward."

old: "The pluperfect (*había empezado*) marks whatever happened before the main story line, while the preterite (*cambié*) carries the story forward — together they let you narrate out of strict chronological order."
new: "The *pluscuamperfecto* (*había empezado*) marks what happened before the main story line, while the *indefinido* (*cambié*) moves the story forward. Together they let you tell a story out of strict order."

old: "Combine opinion, certainty, doubt, evaluation, justification and contrast to explain a position clearly."
new: "You know *no creo que* + subjunctive from B1 Unit 13, *dudo que* from B1 Unit 25, *es importante que* from A2 Unit 27, *aunque* from A2 Unit 28 and *estoy seguro de que* from B1 Unit 67. This lesson combines them to explain a position: opinion, certainty, doubt, evaluation, justification and contrast."

old: "Layering is the skill being tested here: *estoy convencido de que* states a firm view, *porque* justifies it, and a trailing *aunque* clause can concede a limit — three moves in one sentence rather than three separate ones."
new: "Layering is the skill here: *estoy convencido de que* states a firm view, *porque* justifies it and an *aunque* clause concedes a limit. That is three moves in one sentence."

old: "Explain why a problem exists, describe its consequences and propose or evaluate possible solutions."
new: "You know *porque* and *por eso* from A2 Unit 5 and *es necesario que* + subjunctive from A2 Unit 27. This lesson uses them to explain why a problem exists, describe its consequences and propose a solution."

old: "A clear problem-solution paragraph has a natural chain: *porque* names the cause, *por eso* draws out the consequence, and *es necesario que* proposes the fix — writing them in that order rarely goes wrong."
new: "A clear paragraph about a problem follows a chain: *porque* names the cause, *por eso* gives the consequence and *es necesario que* proposes the fix."

old: "Use future, conditional and subjunctive structures to predict, imagine alternatives and discuss uncertain possibilities."
new: "You know the future from A2 Unit 19, *si* + imperfect subjunctive + conditional from B1 Unit 7 and *es posible que* + subjunctive from B1 Unit 25. This lesson uses them to predict, to imagine alternatives and to talk about uncertain possibilities."

old: "Two unrelated 'ifs' live in this unit: *es posible que cambie* is a real possibility (subjunctive, no *si*), while *si hubiera más recursos* is a counterfactual condition (imperfect subjunctive after *si*) — don't let the shared mood make them feel like the same structure."
new: "Two different ideas can look alike: *es posible que cambie* is a real possibility (subjunctive, no *si*), while *si hubiera más recursos* is an imagined condition (imperfect subjunctive after *si*). They share the subjunctive, but not the structure."

old: "Retrieve the main B1 structures in connected communication: narration, opinion, cause, consequence, recommendation, prediction and hypothetical language."
new: "You know the structures of the whole B1 course: narration (B1 Unit 1), opinion and doubt (B1 Units 13 and 25), cause and consequence (A2 Unit 5), recommendation, *si* clauses (B1 Unit 7) and past hypotheticals with *hubiera* (B1 Unit 69). Here you retrieve them together in connected communication."

old: "If one thing is worth rechecking before moving on, it's the indicative/subjunctive split — nearly every structure in this course (opinion, cause, prediction, hypothetical) depends on whether you're stating a fact or something uncertain, evaluated, or unreal."
new: "If one thing deserves a second look, it is the indicative or subjunctive choice: nearly every structure in this unit depends on whether you state a fact or something uncertain, evaluated or unreal."
